## Source 1 — arXiv 2601.19952: LTS-VoiceAgent — Listen-Think-Speak Framework for Efficient Streaming Voice Interaction via Semantic Triggering and Incremental Reasoning

**Type:** Academic paper (arxiv.org/abs/2601.19952, submitted Jan 26 2026)
**Title:** "LTS-VoiceAgent: A Listen-Think-Speak Framework for Efficient Streaming Voice Interaction via Semantic Triggering and Incremental Reasoning"
**Authors:** Wenhao Zou, Yuwei Miao, Zhanyu Ma, Jun Xu, Jiuchong Gao, Jinghua Hao, Renqing He, Jingwen Xu

### Verbatim excerpts:
> "Real-time voice agents face a dilemma: end-to-end models often lack deep reasoning, while cascaded pipelines incur high latency by executing ASR, LLM reasoning, and TTS strictly in sequence, unlike human conversation where listeners often start thinking before the speaker finishes. Since cascaded architectures remain the dominant choice for complex tasks, existing cascaded streaming strategies attempt to reduce this latency via mechanical segmentation (e.g., fixed chunking) ... but these heuristics frequently misalign with semantic boundaries ..."
> "we propose the Listen-Think-Speak (LTS) framework that integrates: (1) semantic end-of-turn prediction triggering LLM reasoning at semantically complete units rather than fixed time windows; (2) an incremental reasoning scheme that begins LLM inference as soon as a semantically complete proposition is detected ..."

### Pain points (verbatim engineering language):
- "mechanical segmentation ... frequently misaligns with semantic boundaries" — the failure mode every voice agent engineer has hit
- "end-to-end models often lack deep reasoning" — the architectural trade-off
- "cascaded architectures remain the dominant choice" — the practical constraint

### Why this works:
The freshest academic signal of the cycle. The LTS framework is the load-bearing engineering insight: don't trigger LLM inference on a fixed chunk or fixed time window — trigger it on a semantic end-of-turn signal. That's the latency win the persona's voice pattern can hang a build-log post on: "My voice agent was chunking audio every 200ms. The persona's first prompt to ASR didn't end at 200ms — it ended at a comma. So the LLM was reading half a sentence and hallucinating. Replaced chunking with semantic-trigger prediction. Latency dropped from 920ms to 640ms. The math is the product." The 4-component architecture (Listen → Think → Speak, with semantic triggering and incremental reasoning) is the framework the persona's audience needs to learn.

## Source 2 — 运行时工程决定Agent未来 (BoxAgnts深度解析) — the runtime vs prompt engineering thesis

**Type:** Engineering blog (cn486.com/news/4134584 — BoxAgnts)
**Headline:** "运行时工程决定Agent未来:BoxAgnts深度解析"

### Verbatim excerpts:
> "过去一年里,AI Agent 项目层出不穷——自主编程助手、浏览器自动化工具、多 Agent 编排框架......每周都有新玩家入场。但一个尴尬的事实是:**大多数 Agent 在生产环境中仍然频繁失败,而且失败的原因惊人地一致——它们缺乏一个可信的运行时。**"
> "提示词工程在 LLM 早期阶段确实不可或缺。通过思维链、ReAct 循环、规划 Agent 等技术,我们大幅提升了模型的推理质量。但这些技术也制造了一个危险的错觉:一旦 Agent 开始与真实系统交互——读写文件、执行命令、调用 API、操作数据库——这个假设瞬间崩塌。**提示词可以影响推理,但提示词无法强制执行安全边界。**"
> "// run_query_loop 的核心逻辑: 1. 向 API 发送对话 2. 处理流式响应 3. 检测工具调用请求并分发执行 4. 将工具结果反馈给模型 5. 处理自动压缩、token 限制恢复、预算超支等边界条件"
> "这个循环暴露了一个根本问题:**模型成为 ...**"

### Pain points (verbatim engineering language):
- "可信的运行时" — the gap that most Agent projects ship without
- "提示词可以影响推理,但提示词无法强制执行安全边界" — the conceptual pivot
- "自动压缩、token 限制恢复、预算超支" — the runtime failure modes that the prompt can't catch

### Why this works:
The 70/30 thesis source. The verbatim "提示词可以影响推理,但提示词无法强制执行安全边界" is the load-bearing line — it's the conceptual move that formalizes the persona's "200 lines Python the wrapper is missing" voice anchor. The runtime loop code (run_query_loop with 5 steps) is the concrete artifact the persona's audience can copy. The narrative: "If your Agent has a 100-line prompt and zero lines of runtime, it will fail in production. Build the wrapper."
